outcome: Head circumference growth patterns (initial size, age of rapid growth, final percentile)
Specific neuroimaging findings (enlarged subarachnoid spaces, dilated lateral ventricles)
cohort: A total of 176 infants (86.4% boys) with benign external hydrocephalus, identified from hospital medical records in two large health regions in Norway, characterized by increasing head circumference and typical radiological findings of enlarged subarachnoid spaces.
finding: Most infants with benign external hydrocephalus are born with a normal head circumference that increases too fast, reaching abnormally high values before age six months, with neuroimaging findings tending to normalize after 12 months.
